name: Purplish Grey
lede: Purplish grey is a plain description: a grey with a tint of purple, with no history of its own.

sections.title: A grey with purple
sections.body:
Paterson uses the phrase in three entries. *Heather* is described as the speckled purplish-grey-blue of the plant [1], and *nugrey* is defined as a purplish-grey [1]. The same dictionary lists plumbago as the purplish grey of graphite [1]. Two of them tie the tone to a plant or a mineral, which is how the language often names such an in-between color [1].

Related names are [[heather]] and [[mauve]] [2]. The phrase itself is a description, not an established color name, so the books tell little else [1]. Paterson uses the phrase as ordinary description inside other entries, not as an entry of its own [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in 19 works, 0.08 per cent of the archive [3]. The earliest is a work of 1375 and the latest dates from 1924 [3]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read them as screen colors [3].
